claims.statement: A refreshed page has one text authority: whatever a receipt or beat renders is a projection of mod text, so editing the page and the mod text independently creates two writers of one sentence.
The ver is a version fingerprint, not an integrity proof: it blanks the token and hashes the rest, so a 6-hex prefix detects change but never proves the reader read the body.
Signature enforcement has four dimensions — coverage, freshness, forgetting, per-person — and dropping any one makes the gate decorative.

The read gate is embedded state (`readGate.window`, default 80 dispatches), not policy read from disk, because the mod has no IO: the ledger records the ver, the window counts the distance, and only a full body read resets it.

The cold-start surface has a hard line budget reported on every run — `agents=<current>/500` today, 160 after the cutover — because an auto-injected surface that grows dilutes every constraint it carries.

Batch settlement sets `docs.maintenance.due=<batch>` inside the same handler transaction as the settled marker, and the next `coordinate.submit` refuses until the obligation is cleared with the equal batch id.
Clearing the obligation is `config.set docs.maintenance.done=<batch>`, and only an equal batch id clears it — an older id cannot, and an empty value is an explicit waiver the writer carries.
`governance` is registered in the `reference` block of the scene table, not in any readPlan, so the rule about how to sign never needs a signature to be read.
